    Class EditHistory

    Linear undo / redo history.

    • push(cmd) records cmd and clears any pending redo entries. It does NOT invoke cmd.do() — the caller is expected to have already performed the work; the command captures what was changed so it can be reversed.
    • undo() invokes cmd.undo() and moves cmd from the undo stack to the redo stack.
    • redo() invokes cmd.do() and moves cmd back onto the undo stack.

    Example

    Runnable example association: attribute-editing, china-editing, draw-snap-clear.

    Methods

    beginCapture

    • beginCapture(): void

      Begin a transaction-style capture session. While active, push(cmd) routes every command into an internal buffer instead of mutating the undo stack, so a multi-step transaction can batch its child commands and present them as a single undo entry on commit.

      Throws if a capture is already in progress — nested transactions are not supported. Pair with endCapture; for safety, transaction code should call endCapture() from a finally-style path so an error in the middle doesn't leave the history stuck in capture mode.

      Returns void

    push

    • push(cmd: EditCommand): void

      Push a new command, evicting the oldest entry if at capacity.

      Merge fast-path: if the top of the undo stack defines a merge companion AND the incoming command's mergeable(top) returns true, the top absorbs the incoming command and nothing is pushed. The redo stack is still cleared (the new edit invalidates forward replay). Used by VertexMoveCommand / FeatureTranslateCommand to coalesce rapid drag / nudge sequences into one undo step.

      If cmd.invalidatesPriorCommands is true (DatasetReplaceCommand), prior undo entries are released and replaced with one lightweight stale boundary before this command is pushed. The command itself remains undoable.

      Parameters

      • cmd: EditCommand

        cmd accepts EditCommand for push. Required; omission is not allowed. Must be assignable to EditCommand.

      Returns void

    redo

    • redo(): EditCommand | null

      Pop the top redo entry, invoke its do(), and move it back to the undo stack. Returns the executed command, or null if there was nothing.

      Stale commands on the redo stack get the same skip semantics as undo() — the redo is a no-op transition because the captured refs are still orphaned even though the entry is moving forward in time.

      Returns EditCommand | null

    undo

    • undo(): EditCommand | null

      Pop the top command, invoke its undo(), and move it to the redo stack. Returns the executed command, or null if there was nothing to undo.

      Stale handling: when the top command's stale flag is true, the command is moved to the redo stack WITHOUT invoking undo() (its captured references point at an object the live dataset no longer uses; running it would write to the wrong place). The skip is reflected in the next snapshot via skippedStale: true. undo() still returns the moved command so callers can detect that a step was traversed.

      Returns EditCommand | null
